headline: Oil falls more than 3% on hopes of US-Iran diplomatic progress
dek: Brent crude fell $3.68 (-3.2%) to $109.75 a barrel by 04:07 GMT and WTI fell $3.43 (-3.3%) to $100.69, as traders cited hopes of progress in indirect US-Iran talks and no meaningful military escalation over the weekend.
sources: Reuters market reporting via Al Jazeera liveblog
fault_line: Does a 3% dip mean the war premium is unwinding, or is $109 oil with tankers still being hit the new normal?

sections.what_happened: Brent crude fell $3.68 (-3.2%) to $109.75 a barrel by 04:07 GMT and WTI fell $3.43 (-3.3%) to $100.69, as traders cited hopes of progress in indirect US-Iran talks and no meaningful military escalation over the weekend.
sections.what_verified: Reuters price print carried by AJ liveblog; independently consistent with Finimize/TradingView Monday oil pieces (Brent $109.75, -3.2%). NOTE: Gulf News liveblog later print (10:11 Beijing time) shows Brent $111.2 / WTI $101.7 - a different timestamp, not a contradiction; the 04:07 GMT print stands.
sections.what_disputed: Prices remain above $100: Brent ended October at its highest in six months and had not dropped below $100 for nearly two weeks (AJ/Bloomberg reporting); tanker attacks continue (Khafji strike Sunday, two Hormuz mine strikes Sunday) and shipping/insurance costs stay elevated even as futures cool.
sections.why_matters: Pocketbook Short: oil dips 3% on talk hopes while tankers are still being hit - the number that matters is still above $100.
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW (AJ liveblog 05:45 GMT = 09:45 ) -- Oil falls more than 3% on hopes of US-Iran diplomatic progress

totw_analysis: Our read: Pocketbook Short: oil dips 3% on talk hopes while tankers are still being hit - the number that matters is still above $100. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Does a 3% dip mean the war premium is unwinding, or is $109 oil with tankers still being hit the new normal?
